chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh and Sindi ibn Muhammad from Safwan ibn Yahya from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman who had a husband, and he did not know. He said, 'The woman is slapped (or struck), and there is no penalty upon the man if he did not know.'
He said, So I mentioned that to Abu Basir. He said to me, 'By Allah, Ja'far (peace be upon him) said,
The woman is slapped, and the man is flogged with the prescribed punishment.
He said, placing his hands on my chest and scratching it,
I do not think our Master (the Imam) had fully perfected his knowledge (in this specific ruling).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between what Shu'ayb narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and what Abu Basir heard from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), because the one who asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) may have married the woman while not knowing she had a husband, so he was given the ruling that there was no penalty upon him. And what Abu Basir heard from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) concerns the one who married her while knowing she had a husband and consummated the marriage, so he also imposed the flogging upon him because this is adultery. There is no contradiction between the two narrations and the two rulings; rather, the matter became confused upon Abu Basir, so he did not distinguish between one of the two questions from the other, and he thought there was a contradiction between them.

key_terms.الْحَدَّ: The prescribed legal punishment in Islamic law.
key_terms.تُرْجَمُ: To be slapped or struck lightly on the face/head, a minor punishment.
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: To be flogged or beaten with a whip.

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a man who marries a woman while she is already married to someone else?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between Imam al-Rida’s ruling of no penalty and Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling of hadd by distinguishing between ignorance (jahil) and knowledge (ilm) of the woman's existing marriage. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the severity of the penalty for temporary or permanent marriage with a married woman depends on the man's awareness of her marital status. The narration underscores the importance of precise conditions in deriving legal rulings from seemingly conflicting hadiths.
